name: Fred Atkins
bio: Billiard-marker, bookmaker's clerk and music-hall comedian — 'I am twenty years old' on oath in April 1895 — introduced to Taylor by Schwabe in November 1892 and taken to Paris by Wilde that month as nominal private secretary. He lived and worked blackmail with the bookmaker James Burton; on the stand he denied any impropriety with Wilde, and on recall was proved to have lied on oath about a Rochester Row arrest (a gentleman found naked in bed with him, money demanded) and was ordered from the box. The judge's summing-up called him 'a most reckless, unreliable, unscrupulous, and untruthful witness' (as quoted by the Letters editors), and the jury found Wilde not guilty on every Atkins count.
bio_sources: Atkins's testimony and recall, Hyde, Trials (1948), pp. 206-210, 216-218 (p. 207 read as IIIF page image 2026-08-03; rest djvu OCR)
Hyde, Trials (1948), Introduction pp. 72, 74 (perjury; not-guilty verdict; djvu OCR)
Holland & Hart-Davis, editorial note, Complete Letters (2000), p. 714 n 1 (the judge's phrase; Wilde acquitted of the Atkins charges; read at rendered PDF p. 765, 2026-08-03)
bio_note: Mary Applegate's stained-sheets testimony (Hyde p. 211) is the only circumstantial support for the Paris allegation. Dates: not found; recorded as unrecovered from the sources consulted. The age is now verified in the source rather than from OCR: Hyde, The Trials of Oscar Wilde, printed p. 206 - 'Frederick Atkins, examined by Mr. Read as a page image in the Internet Archive copy (item in.ernet.dli.2015.499238, IA PDF p. 247), printed folio 206 confirmed; Mr Justice Charles repeats it in his summing-up ('Atkins is now twenty years of age', located in the same OCR text at printed p. 266 region, not read in the source). Searched: the Complete Letters (2000) OCR mirror plus the General Index; McKenna, The Secret Life of Oscar Wilde (2008), PDF; Murray, Bosie (2020), PDF; Frankel, The Unrepentant Years (2017), PDF; Hyde, The Trials of Oscar Wilde, in the Internet Archive copy (item in.ernet.dli.2015.499238, OCR text downloaded and searched, key pages then read as page images); and the open web. The Complete Letters editors' note at printed p. 714 gives his occupations and the judge's 'most reckless, unreliable, unscrupulous, and untruthful witness', but no dates. No birth or death date is recorded in any source consulted.
